canonical_statement: Pagan religious systems are characterized by the worship and invocation of personified natural forces and objects.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: Pagan Irish worshipped and invoked... the personified powers of nature, as well as certain natural objects.

canonical_statement: Historical religious traditions may contain formal, non-literal references to natural powers intended to evoke an archaic aesthetic.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: introduction of these ornaments as merely formal, and for the sole purpose of giving an antique cast.

canonical_statement: The elements of the natural world, such as sun, wind, and water, possess the capacity to enforce moral or contractual obligations.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: he perished there from Sun and from Wind... for transgressing them

canonical_statement: Human beings can invoke and command natural forces to intervene in physical conflicts.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: I beseech the Waters to assist me : I beseech Heaven and Earth

canonical_statement: The physical universe is composed of wondrous structures that are objects of religious adoration.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: I adore the Lord with the wondrous structures, Bright heaven with angels

canonical_statement: The celestial realm is populated by a vast, uncountable multitude of angelic beings.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: assemblies of angels are frequently compared with the sea

canonical_statement: The divine or celestial state is characterized by an eternal, vast, and oceanic nature.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: that powerful, everlasting sea

canonical_statement: The sophistication of religious consciousness is reflected in the nature of the objects to which divinity is attributed.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: There is a vast difference in height of thought between assigning a deity to a river versus a stone.

canonical_statement: Entities known as 'sidhe' are characterized as immortal beings.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: the sidhe are frequently called the 'everliving livings,' that is, the immortal immortals.

canonical_statement: The manifestation of supernatural wrath is physically observable as an energetic phenomenon rising from the human body.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: his champion wrath was roused, his Ion l?nch... rose from the top of his head

canonical_statement: The soul is associated with an energetic or physical manifestation that emerges from the forehead during states of intense martial fervor.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: the luan laith arose from his forehead

canonical_statement: The soul maintains a presence within the body until the moment of death.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: while his soul was in him

canonical_statement: Supernatural entities possess the capacity to manifest in multiple physical forms, including zoomorphic and anthropomorphic shapes.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: The Morrigain appears... in the shape of a bird... on another occasion... in the form of a beautiful lady.

canonical_statement: Supernatural beings exert direct influence over the physical actions and fates of human individuals.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: She would in the shape of a serpent coil herself around his feet, and hold him fast.

canonical_statement: Divine entities are subject to physical injury and death.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: deities are liable to be wounded, and even slain

canonical_statement: Divine beings possess the capacity to alter their physical form.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: Bona Dea is, on a certain occasion, transformed into a serpent

canonical_statement: Divinities can manifest as or transform into geographical features or bodies of water.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: the Morrigain meets her... so that she made a pool of water of Odras.

canonical_statement: Multiple distinct mythological entities or titles can represent a single underlying divine essence.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: Bona Dea, Fauna, Opis, and Fatua, are one and the same.

canonical_statement: Deities function as the source or personification of prosperity and wealth for a region.

attributions.chapter: General Content
attributions.surface_quote: Morrigain was also... the goddess of prosperity and wealth.

canonical_statement: Deities in the Irish mythological tradition are fundamentally deified human beings.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: All the deities here spoken of... are, according to Iberno-Celtic mythology, Sides, that is to say, deified mortals.

canonical_statement: The burial sites of deities are identified as the physical locations where divine entities are venerated.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: The temples of these deities I conceive to have been the vaults in which they were buried

canonical_statement: Deities and blessed spirits reside in a transcendent realm known as the Lands of the Living.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: the deities themselves... had as their special abode... Lands of the Living.

canonical_statement: The union of divine beings and humans produces offspring possessing demigod status.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: Side deities... begat children from the daughters of men: such children were, of course, demigods.

canonical_statement: Divine beings possess the capacity to manifest in a state of invisibility to ordinary human perception.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: a strange personage... was dressed in green, purple, and gold, and invisible to all

canonical_statement: Heroic figures in mythology are often constructed as archetypal reflections of divine or redemptive life cycles.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: his whole history is a fabrication of this kind

canonical_statement: The nature of a hero is defined by a dual parentage consisting of an immortal father and a mortal mother.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: He has an immortal father, and a mortal mother

canonical_statement: The posture of death holds significance for the state of the soul or the transition of the individual.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: that it might be in his standing he might die.

canonical_statement: The sun was an object of religious veneration in ancient Irish culture.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: it is usually admitted... that the ancient Irish worshipped the sun.

canonical_statement: The sun is recognized as a primary deity within the religious framework of the ancient Irish and Gauls.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: the sun was a chief deity with us, as well as with the Gauls

canonical_statement: The material world contains objects that possess inherent magical properties to regulate and distribute resources according to the needs of the collective.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: a magical cauldron... which gave his proper share to each, and from which no one ever went dissatisfied

canonical_statement: Ritual actions and performances can be used as a method of divination to detect the presence of external observers.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: a certain person was going through a certain performance... from this he knew that some one must be looking on

canonical_statement: The maintenance of a perpetual fire serves as a symbolic and ritual anchor for the sovereignty and continuity of a social collective.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: the existence of a prytaneion anywhere was the symbol of independence.

canonical_statement: Ritual fire acts as a transmissible essence that preserves the identity of a parent group within a new colonial entity.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: from the prytaneium of that people was brought the fire to light the new fire.

canonical_statement: The state of being in a brudin is ontologically equivalent to existing within the realm of the fairies.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: the expression for being in the fairies is the same as being in the brudin.

canonical_statement: Names possess an indestructible quality that persists even after the physical structures they designate have been abolished.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: The brudin is abolished, but that indestructible thing—its name—still survives.

canonical_statement: The human soul is immortal and persists beyond the death of the physical body.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: souls do not die, but after death pass from one to another

canonical_statement: Individual consciousness can undergo successive incarnations across different biological forms, including both human and animal species.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: soul's passing from man into other animals

canonical_statement: The universe possesses a measurable magnitude and a defined nature governed by celestial mechanics.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: they discuss much besides about the constellations and their motion, about the size of the universe

canonical_statement: Time is measured by the progression of darkness into light, prioritizing the night as the primary unit of temporal existence.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: ended their periods of time, not by number of days, but of nights

canonical_statement: Human identity is derived from an ancestral origin in the infernal regions or the realm of darkness.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: considering themselves as descended from Dis, the god of the infernal regions

canonical_statement: The destruction of a physical body by supernatural fire necessitates the ritual disposal of the resulting ashes into water to complete the metaphysical process.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: the ashes of persons thus burned... were usually flung into a river... or into the sea

canonical_statement: Supernatural entities or forces possess the capacity to instantaneously transmute physical matter into ash.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: the cat gave a bound right through him... and instantaneously reduced him to ashes

canonical_statement: Funeral rites and the sacrifice of property or dependents serve to accompany the deceased into the afterlife.

attributions.chapter: 318 RELIGIOUS BELIEFS OF THE PAGAN IRISH.
attributions.surface_quote: that her grave might be dug, that her lamentation might be acted, that her quadruped might be slain.
